title: Balanced equations and reacting masses
specRef: C1.1(a), C1.1(c), C1.3(j), C1.6(r) and others
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM07#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM07#N.4a, AM07#N.6a, AM07#N.12a, AM07#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: A solid formed when two solutions react, e.g. AgCl from Ag⁺ and Cl⁻.

items.label: State symbols
items.clue: The labels (s), (l), (g) and (aq) written after each species in an equation.

items.label: Coefficient
items.clue: A number that multiplies a whole formula and gives the ratio of amounts in moles.

items.label: Spectator ions
items.clue: Dissolved species that appear unchanged on both sides of an equation and are left out.

questions.stem: Aluminium burns in oxygen to form aluminium oxide. Which equation for this reaction is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: Al₂O₃ and O₂ are the right formulae. 3O₂ gives 6 O = 2Al₂O₃, which needs 4Al. 4 Al and 6 O each side.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon fizzes and dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid. Which is the ionic equation for the reaction?
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ is a spectator. 1 Mg and 2 H each side; charge 2+ each side.

questions.stem: Iron is produced by reducing iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g). What is the maximum mass of iron that can be produced from 40.0 g of iron(III) oxide? (Ar: O 16.0, Fe 55.8)
A strip of magnesium burns brightly in air and leaves white magnesium oxide: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s). What mass of MgO forms from 2.43 g of Mg? (Ar: O 16.0, Mg 24.3)
